takeaway: Low calcium makes chief cells release PTH, which stimulates 1α-hydroxylase in the kidney to activate vitamin D, and reduces renal phosphate reabsorption.

question.text: Which of the following statements regarding calcium homeostasis is true?
question.say: Which of the following statements regarding calcium homeostasis is true?

lines.text: Calcium is controlled by parathormone, calcitonin and vitamin D. Here the calcium level has fallen.
The chief cells of the parathyroid gland sense the fall and ring the alarm, releasing parathormone, PTH.
In the kidney, PTH stimulates the enzyme one alpha hydroxylase, the little robot with the wrench.
It turns dull vitamin D into active vitamin D, and plasma calcium rises.
PTH also reduces phosphate reabsorption in the kidney, so phosphate leaves in the urine.
So the true statement is that parathormone stimulates one alpha hydroxylase.
